extracted.intended_audience: journal editors, peer reviewers, researchers of peer review, and policy makers concerned with editorial practice
extracted.subtask_description: Standards, evaluation dimensions, and recommended procedures for conducting, studying, and improving journal manuscript peer review (including reviewer rating scales, editorial responsibilities, reviewer accountability, and ethical constraints).

rubrics_metrics.name: 4-point summary decision scale
rubrics_metrics.description: A 4-point global summary judgment for manuscripts: accept as is; accept with revisions; reject but encourage resubmission; reject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as a concise overall recommendation. In the reported data the 4-point summary judgment was at least as reliable as many multi-item scales; some multi-item scales were less reliable or completely unreliable compared to this summary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall quality (7-point rating)
rubrics_metrics.description: A 7-point Likert rating of the manuscript's overall quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC) = .25 in the study. Part of a 10-dimension rating form; nevertheless, this scale was not significantly more reliable than the 4-point summary judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact (citations/controversy) (7-point rating)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rating of the expected impact of the manuscript measured by likely citations or controversy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported ICC = .20. Intended to capture downstream influence but showed modest reliability in this data set.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conceptualization of problem (7-point rating)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rating of how well the manuscript conceptualizes the research problem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported ICC = .09, indicating low interrater reliability for this dimension in the reported sample.

rubrics_metrics.name: Importance of topic (7-point rating)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rating of the topical importance or significance of the manuscript's subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported ICC = −.01 (near zero/negative), suggesting little to no agreement among reviewers on this dimension in the studied sample.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality of treatment (7-point rating)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rating of the originality or novelty in the manuscript's approach or treatment of the topic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported ICC = .29. One of the more reliable of the ten specific dimensions but still not clearly superior to the 4-point summary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality of writing (7-point rating)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rating of the clarity, style, and technical quality of the writing/presentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported ICC = .15. Note that editorial and reviewer judgments are sensitive to presentation changes; 'cosmetic' alterations can affect perceived quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theoreticality (7-point rating)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rating of the manuscript's theoretical contribution or theoretical grounding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported ICC = .31 — the highest among these dimensions in the reported data — but still not necessarily more reliable than a global summary judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reliability of results (7-point rating)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rating of the methodological reliability or robustness of the manuscript's empirical results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported ICC = .20. Intended to capture methodological soundness; reliability varied across reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validity of conclusions (7-point rating)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rating of whether the authors' conclusions are justified by the data and analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported ICC = .22. Part of the 10-dimension battery; showed modest interrater agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Breadth of interested audience (7-point rating)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rating of the extent to which the manuscript will interest a broad audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported ICC = .01, indicating very low interrater agreement on this dimension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use a standard rating form with explicit criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt a standardized reviewer rating form that enumerates explicit dimensions and criteria for evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggested to improve consistency and make review bases explicit. The empirical test in the article used 10 dimensions on such a form, but many scales were no more reliable than a global summary — design of scales matters and some dimensions may be inherently unreliable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author ratings of reviewers (fairness/carefulness/constructiveness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Have submitting authors evaluate reviewers on dimensions such as fairness, carefulness, and constructiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed to increase reviewer accountability. In a trial, less than 20% of authors returned such forms, reducing feasibility; concerns exist about validity akin to student evaluations of teachers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide reviewers with training/information from editors
rubrics_metrics.description: Supply referees with training materials and clearer instructions from editors to increase review reliability and validity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Endorsed as likely beneficial though some reviewers may resent it. Training could improve consistency; however implementation may prompt some to resign.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editors should evaluate reviewers' substantive comments (editor as judge)
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors must assess and weigh the substantive quality of reviewers' comments rather than rely solely on summary recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Given low reviewer reliability, editorial judgment is crucial. Editors should act as judges between reviews and author responses and may need to take an active role in resolving mixed reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow author rebuttal and reconsideration (relax 'judges' decision final')
rubrics_metrics.description: Permit rebuttal letters and requests for reconsideration from authors rather than a rigid 'decision final' policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Would let authors contest decisions in a structured way; could improve fairness but must be managed to avoid undue reward for aggressiveness rather than merit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid signed reviews as a general requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Caution against mandatory signed reviews because they may reduce frank criticism and decrease willingness to review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some reviewers sign voluntarily and remain frank, but most may decline to submit signed reviews; the practical outcome could be fewer available reviewers and possible bias in who accepts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select reviewers conversant with the literature (broad and appropriate reviewer pool)
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose reviewers who are knowledgeable about the specific literature (e.g., textbook or review authors) rather than relying only on prominent researchers who may not follow narrow literatures closely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expanding reviewer pools to include people more conversant with the literature may reduce failures to detect redundancy or prior publication. Editors should cultivate knowledge of who knows what.

rubrics_metrics.name: Increase the number and diversity of reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Use larger and more diverse reviewer pools to reduce misses in detecting prior publication or errors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Larger reviewer stables may increase the chance that someone familiar with the prior literature sees redundancy, but practical constraints exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editors should avoid biased reviewer assignment (conflict of interest avoidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Refrain from assigning friends or lenient reviewers to favorable treatment; assign reviewers to avoid nepotism and bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial practices range from assigning strongest manuscripts to strongest reviewers to the pernicious practice of assigning friends to lenient reviewers; this impacts fairness and must be guarded against.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require reviewers to rate currency/redundancy explicitly
rubrics_metrics.description: Ask reviewers to evaluate whether a submission is current, redundant, or previously published as an explicit review dimension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Would help determine whether lack of currency contributed to rejections; authors suggested this would have clarified whether reviewers correctly judged resubmitted published work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure research on peer review follows appropriate controls and design
rubrics_metrics.description: When studying peer review, include appropriate control groups and multifactorial designs (e.g., author status X institution prestige X reviewer status X blind vs. nonblind) to avoid invalid inferences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: P & C acknowledged limitations of quasi-experimental designs and recommended grand designs that require editorial cooperation. Researchers should avoid selective literature citation and test alternative explanations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obtain informed consent / avoid deceptive experimentation on editors and reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not experiment on editors or reviewers without informed consent; deceptive practices that use bogus papers and involve editors/reviewers without consent raise ethical concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critics argued that time was 'stolen' from unwitting participants and that deception leading to negative portrayal of subjects violates ethical norms. If research must deceive, ethical justification and safeguards are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure reliability/ecological validity across the entire editorial process
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess interrater reliability with repeated measures that span the entire editorial process (reviewers, editor decisions, possible correspondence with authors) rather than isolated reviewer agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No studies have fully measured reliability of the whole process; comprehensive (ecologically valid) repeated-measures designs are desirable though difficult to collect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewers should provide educative, substantive feedback, not just summary pronouncements
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews should include clear explanations of reasons for acceptance/rejection and educational comments to help authors improve, not merely terse negative verdicts or cover letters that assert reviewer wisdom.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors and reviewers should realize that an educational role is part of their duties; cover letters praising reviewers' wisdom may mask lack of substantive evidence and are not excusable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competency testing for reviewers and editors
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate and, where feasible, test the competence of reviewers and editors to ensure they can judge imaginative or technical work appropriately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concerns raised that imaginative investigators lack peers and that reviewers/editors sometimes demonstrate incompetence; competency testing or selection procedures may help ensure adequate editorial competence.
